notes:
Key summary: Veridian is a mid-to-large fintech building a consumer lending platform. Strong emphasis on encryption posture and key ownership. Wants Private (VPC) deployment — not comfortable with hosted control plane unless BYOK + HSM validated. Important snippets from calls:
- 'We need proof that we can rotate keys without downtime' (Head of Security)
- Wants TLS mutual auth between customer network and Redwood control plane endpoints, prefer mTLS with client certs rotated on a 90-day cadence.
POC success criteria (stated):
- Demonstrate BYOK integration with customer KMS (AWS KMS + optional Azure Key Vault), including CMK rotation and successful re-encryption of a test dataset
- Show audit logs exported to their SIEM (Splunk) with immutable retention and at least 1 year retention
- Verify no plaintext model tokens or secrets written to logs or object storage; secrets must be vaulted and ephemeral credentials enforced
Notes: legal is pushing for HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2/3) + proof of key destruction for decommission. Compliance will require SOC2/ISO evidence and an annual external pentest report. Infrastructure prefers envelope encryption: DEK encrypted with customer KEK in their KMS. They expect Redwood to support both Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) and Bring-Your-Own-HSM (BYOH).
encryption_posture_summary: In-transit: require TLS1.3, mTLS for control-plane endpoints with client cert provisioning via SCEP/ACME or manual cert upload; cipher suites limited to AEAD (CHACHA20_POLY1305, AES-GCM). Termination options discussed: customer-side mTLS to a private ingress (preferred) or mutual TLS into Redwood control plane with customer certs rotated every 90 days. At-rest: envelope encryption model. Customer-managed CMK (AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault) used to protect DEKs; DEKs stored encrypted in the private control plane database and rotated on schedule. Key rotation: support automated re-encryption of active DEKs when CMK rotates, documented runbook; recommended DEK rotation window 30–90 days, CMK rotation per customer's policy but Redwood must support rotation without service interruption. Secrets management: integrate with HashiCorp Vault or native KMS for secret fetch; ephemeral credentials (STS-style) for node access, no long-lived static tokens; secrets not logged; secret zeroing in memory after use. HSM/BYOH: support for import of HSM-backed keys or external key references (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM) to satisfy FIPS requirements. Audit logging: comprehensive, immutable audit trail for key usage, admin actions, and API calls; logs must be exportable to customer SIEM (Splunk, S3/GCS) with retention policy configurable (default 1 year). Data residency: production datasets must remain in US-only regions; cross-region replication only after approval. Additional controls: token-level telemetry to help debug without exposing content, ability to redact sensitive fields before logs leave VPC.
